title: Applications of Differentiation
seo_title: Applications of Calculus – SSS 3 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Find turning points and say whether they are maxima or minima; find equations of tangents; solve rate of change, velocity and optimisation problems. (summary of the NERDC SSS 3 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free SSS 3 maths worksheets on applications of differentiation: turning points, maxima and minima, tangents, velocity and acceleration, and rates of change. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Set dy/dx = 0 and solve to find the x-values of the turning points.
  • Use the second derivative: positive means a minimum, negative means a maximum.
  • If s is distance, v = ds/dt is velocity and a = dv/dt is acceleration.

Examples

Example

y = x² − 6x + 5

2x − 6 = 0, x = 3

y = −4

Answer: Minimum at (3, −4)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Giving only x for a turning pointFind y too.
Mixing up maximum and minimumCheck the sign of d²y/dx².
Using the curve’s y for the tangent gradientGradient = dy/dx at that point.

items.q: Find the turning point of y = 2x² + 8x + 6 and say whether it is a maximum or a minimum.
items.e: dy/dx = 4x + 8 = 0 gives x = −2, and y = −2. d²y/dx² = 4 is positive, so it is a minimum.

items.q: A body moves so that its distance s metres after t seconds is s = t² + 4t + 11. Find its velocity when t = 4.

items.q: Find the rate of change of the volume of a sphere with respect to its radius when r = 6 cm.
items.e: V = (4/3)πr³, so dV/dr = 4πr² = 144π cm³/cm.

items.q: Find the absolute minimum value of f(x) = 2x² − 4x − 5 on [0, 4].
items.e: Compare f at x = 1, 0 and 4: −7, −5, 11. The smallest is −7.

items.q: Find the absolute maximum value of f(x) = 3x² + 18x + 18 on [−6, 1].
items.e: Check the critical point x = −3 and the end points: f = −9, 18, 39. The largest is 39.

items.q: Two positive numbers have sum 16. Find the largest possible value of their product.
items.e: P = x(16 − x); dP/dx = 16 − 2x = 0 gives x = 8, so the maximum product is 8 × 8 = 64.

items.q: Equal squares are cut from the corners of a 12 cm square sheet, and the sides are folded up to make an open box. What side of square gives the largest volume?
items.e: V = x(12 − 2x)²; dV/dx = 0 gives x = 2 (the other root 6 gives no box). 2 cm, volume 128 cm³.

items.q: Two positive numbers have sum 12. Find the largest possible value of their product.
items.e: P = x(12 − x); dP/dx = 12 − 2x = 0 gives x = 6, so the maximum product is 6 × 6 = 36.

items.q: Find the minimum value of x + 4/x for x > 0.
items.e: f′ = 1 − 4/x² = 0 at x = 2; f″ > 0, so the minimum is 2 + 2 = 4.
